newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT:Goldman/Kotak lower India TISCO net.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT:Goldman/Kotak lower India TISCO net.

text.p: Kotak Securities and its affiliate Goldman Sachs on Tuesday lowered their 1997/98 (April-March) earnings growth estimates for Indian steelmaker Tata Iron & Steel Company (TISCO).

"Steel demand will likely be weak (only 4.0 percent growth) during first half 1997/98 because of the high inventories currently with producers and users," analysts Sandeep Neema and Anand Aithal said in a report.
They said demand growth for steel was expected to climb to 6.0 percent during the second half of the current financial year and to 7.5 percent by 1998/99.

"However, the modestly improving demand outlook may not translate into pricing flexibility for domestic manufacturers, especially of hot rolled coils (HRC) because of rising supply in 1998/99," the report said.
The report said domestic HRC output was expected to jump by 2.1 million tonnes over the next 24 months.
HRC is the major product category of TISCO -- India's largest private steelmaker.

Neema and Aithal said they lowered their 1997/98 earnings growth estimates to 13.4 percent, from 17.4 percent to reflect weak price trends. They cut their net profit forecast for that year to 7.19 billion rupees, from 7.42 billion.
They forecast a net profit of 6.32 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, 1997, down from 6.7 billion the previous year.
The analysts said rising inventories with users would restrict demand growth in 1997/98.
"There could be room for an earnings surprise on the upside if there are any startup delays in the new projects, or international prices increase significantly," they said.

They said the upside in international HRC prices -- which rose 5.0-7.0 percent during the quarter ended March 1997 to $310 per tonne -- was likely to be capped by capacity expansions in the U.S., Korea, Taiwan and other countries.
"We expect global HRC prices to increase modestly (less than 10 percent) in 1997 and trend downward in 1998 as a result of new capacity."
The analysts said TISCO's price to earnings multiples for 1996/97 and 1997/98 compared favourably with regional and global steel producers.
"A fiscal 1997 price to cash flow multiple of 5.4 times also appears favorable."
